summary: Radar for 2026-11-15, GLP-1 focus. ObesityWeek (Nov 14–17) is the main news driver, with Lilly releasing data on EloraTZP, retatrutide (TRIUMPH-1 sleep apnea and knee pain) and teen Zepbound, plus a Cleveland Clinic real-world analysis of what happens after stopping. The FDA's class-wide NAION eye warning (Nov 9) is still spreading through mainstream news (ABC Nov 14, The Hill, NeurologyLive, Fox affiliates). Most coverage is news articles rather than calm, label-based explainers aimed at tirzepatide users, so the gap is there. The best new hook is a Nature Metabolism paper (Nov 13): carriers of rare damaging GLP1R variants lost 2.4% vs 8.8% on semaglutide but 13.3% vs 15.2% on tirzepatide. It is a genetic, non-randomized analysis, so it fits a Short or a chapter in a broad 'why it works differently' video better than a single-study long-form. Evergreen search formats still lead for long-form: first-month timeline, keeping results after stopping, the eye-warning label change, pen how-to, hair loss and nausea. Thanksgiving fullness Shorts start Nov 18 for the Nov 18–27 peak. No fresh randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide surfaced in the last 48 h. CagriSema REDEFINE 4 is the one to watch at ObesityWeek, but I couldn't verify a full presentation. Rejected: GLP-1 microdosing for longevity (SciAm), the compounded-additive study, black-market jab stories, and cost or coverage news. The EloraTZP sales-rep lawsuit, Deloitte coverage cuts and DJ Khaled's Wegovy campaign are also off-brand.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) eye warning explained: the FDA's class-wide NAION label change, and which sudden vision changes mean get care right away
candidates.angle: A calm 'label change explained' long-form. What NAION is (sudden, painless vision loss in one eye). What the FDA's review found: about 6.4 vs 3.8 cases per 100,000 person-years across 126 trials. Why 'rare' and 'potential increased risk' are the right words. The exact symptoms that mean urgent care. Questions to ask your prescriber or eye doctor. Fear-free and no stopping advice.
candidates.predicted_peak: now to 7 days (long tail for months as patients read the new label)
candidates.why_now: The FDA required the warning on Nov 9. Mainstream pickup is still growing: ABC Nov 14, NeurologyLive Nov 13, The Hill op-ed 'risk of blindness… too serious to ignore', Fox affiliates. Patients are seeing scary headlines and searching for what it means for tirzepatide specifically. Label-change explainers are one of the owner's 10x–195x search formats.

evidence.signal: FDA requires class-wide GLP-1 RA labeling change for potential NAION risk (Nov 9)
126 trials, 134,000+ patients; 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 per year
Added to Warnings and Precautions for all GLP-1 medicines including Mounjaro/Zepbound

candidates.topic: Keeping results after stopping tirzepatide: what SURMOUNT-4 shows, refreshed by the Cleveland Clinic real-world analysis at ObesityWeek (Nov 14)
candidates.angle: A broad evergreen video. Lead with randomized evidence: SURMOUNT-4 had 335 vs 335 participants, placebo regained 14.0% on average, yet still ended 9.9% below baseline. Then the real-world note, clearly labelled observational: in about 8,000 patients, people who kept up some form of ongoing obesity care did better. Message: plan any change with your prescriber. Never frame switching or stopping as advice.
keywords: what happens when you stop zepbound
candidates.predicted_peak: now and January (resolution and coverage-change season)
candidates.why_now: Several independent signals: Cleveland Clinic newsroom and Healio Nov 14, Medical Daily on an unreviewed regain analysis (Nov 13), Fox News '6 rebound risks' (Nov 12), and Ars Technica on people not taking GLP-1s as prescribed. candidates.topic: Why semaglutide may not work for some people but tirzepatide might: rare GLP1R gene variants (Nature Metabolism, Nov 13)
candidates.angle: The 'why does it work differently for different people?' question, made concrete. In 13,725 treated adults, carriers of rare damaging GLP1R variants lost 2.4% vs 8.8% on semaglutide but 13.3% vs 15.2% on tirzepatide. Explain the dual GIP + GLP-1 mechanism simply. Be clear it's a genetic association study: these variants are rare, routine testing isn't standard, and response questions go to your prescriber. A tirzepatide-first title.
candidates.predicted_peak: 5–14 days (science press is picking it up; creators haven't yet)
candidates.why_now: Nature Metabolism published two companion papers on Nov 12–13, and science press (Bioengineer) picked them up, but there's almost no creator coverage yet. It answers a high-volume felt question ('why isn't it working for me?') and strengthens the tirzepatide head-to-head lane in an obesity-adjacent population.

evidence.signal: Rare GLP1R variants attenuate weight loss with semaglutide but not tirzepatide
Rare GLP1R variants diminish semaglutide effect but not tirzepatide

candidates.topic: EloraTZP at ObesityWeek: 23.3% weight loss in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes, plus the food-noise and cravings data
candidates.angle: A follow-up for our biggest earner's audience: what's confirmed from the Phase 2 data Lilly presented. Adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes lost 23.3% on average at 48 weeks, with A1C down up to 2.9%. In eloralintide participants, 74% reported fewer cravings and 52% less food noise. It's investigational and isn't approved. Close by linking the original EloraTZP video.
candidates.why_now: Lilly's ObesityWeek release went out Nov 14. 'eloralintide' and 'eloratzp' are our proven search terms, and EloraTZP has earned 4,598 min. Its daily minutes are falling, so a fresh, linked follow-up can revive the cluster.

evidence.signal: New data across Zepbound, Foundayo, EloraTZP and retatrutide at ObesityWeek 2026
EloraTZP Phase 2: 54.1 lb (23.3%) average at 48 weeks in T2D

candidates.topic: Lifting weights on tirzepatide: the T-REx randomized trial (Nature Medicine, Nov 9) on keeping muscle
candidates.angle: Practical and encouraging. In adults aged 50–70 without type 2 diabetes, resistance training during tirzepatide treatment limited lean-mass loss and improved strength with similar weight loss. What 'resistance training 3 times a week' looked like, in plain terms. Exact populations and measures, verified from the paper. Funnel to the Strength and Bones & Muscle long-forms.
candidates.why_now: Pickup is spreading from the journal to consumer outlets: News-Medical (Nov 12), MindBodyGreen 'one nutrient… muscle' (Nov 12), and Korean press on muscle loss (Nov 14). The Lancet COURAGE muscle-preservation trial (Nov 11) keeps 'muscle on GLP-1' in the news.

evidence.signal: RCT: resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy
